title: Graceful spill and compact-revivor for paged KV
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Design and implement a graceful spill + compact-revivor strategy for the paged KV cache that reduces decode tail latency and fragmentation overhead under tenant contention. The feature has three coordinated parts: (1) a fair-share spill policy that routes low-touch fragments to host RAM or local SSD instead of immediate eviction, (2) a background compaction/rehydration agent (compact-revivor) that merges adjacent small fragments into coalesced slots during low-util windows, and (3) a prefill/prefill-credit merging mechanism that paces decode prefill work and signals kernel-selection hints when fragments are sparse so the runtime prefers sparse-attention kernels for fragmented batches. The goal is to lower 95th/99th percentile prefill latency by 15-30% on mixed-tenant workloads while keeping GPU memory pressure predictable.
comments: 2026-02-10 Aisha Raman: Created ticket after postmortem on incident #INC-2026-011 where aggressive eviction under tenant spike caused decode latency cliffs. Linked incident notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-011 and dashboard snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kv-incident/kv-evict?from=16400

2026-02-13 Marco Li: Spike repro script added and measured baseline: mixed-tenant replay with 200 concurrent sessions shows 99p prefill latency increase from 210ms -> 780ms when cache crosses 78% occupancy. Baseline kernels: dense-attn for contiguous fragments; fallback to fallback-decoder for sparse pages.

2026-02-20 Marco Li: Prototype fair-spill policy implemented (host RAM spill + tenant-weighted queue). Early microbench: 20% reduction in 99p latency in synthetic tests but 4% higher average CPU usage on host due to copy/serialize to spill store. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1934

2026-02-24 Review (Design): Sofia Alvarez: Concern about increased I/O during compaction windows; recommended adding adaptive compaction thresholds and low-priority IO class. Also asked to surface tenant spill events to Console (rollups + alerting).

2026-02-27 Marco Li: Added compact-revivor design doc and scheduler: compact-revivor triggers when contiguous free-fragment ratio > 12% and GPU idle < 25% for 120s. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Compact-Reviver-Design. Started unit tests for fragment merge correctness.

2026-03-03 Engineering sync: Decision to use two-phase rehydration: (1) best-effort in-memory merge without blocking prefill, (2) opportunistic full rewrite to compact slab when a quota of merges pending >= 16. Tradeoffs: slightly increased memory churn vs. fewer future prefill misses.

2026-03-06 Marco Li: Kernel-hinting API added: runtime emits FRAGMENT_PENALTY score per request, scheduler prefers sparse-attn kernels when score > 0.6. Benchmarks with quantized models show sparse kernels reduce token decode CPU by ~18% for highly fragmented batches.

2026-03-09 QA: Integration test failure observed under many small rehydrations: occasionally prefill credit merging delays new requests causing head-of-line blocking. Temporarily disabled full-rewrite step and increased credit-window to 8 microbatches. Created follow-up ENG-305679 to investigate scheduler starvation patterns.

2026-03-12 Marco Li: Updated strategy after profiling: add backpressure token to prefill admission that gates background compaction; this reduces priority inversion. Next steps: finalize metrics, add Console panels for spill/compact events, and run canary on dedicated pool. Canary plan: 3-week ramp starting 2026-03-22 against runtime-1.25

Reviewer notes: PR feedback from L. Chen — ensure compaction respects tenant isolation (do not coalesce fragments across tenant boundaries). Security review: no secrets involved; disk spill encrypted by KMS via existing runtime integration.
acceptance_criteria: 95th prefill latency <= baseline * 0.85 on mixed-tenant replay at 200 concurrency
No cross-tenant coalescence of fragments (validate with unit tests)
Console surfaces spill/revive events and a latency regression alert in rollout
Background compaction IO limited to low-priority class and configurable via runtime config
No increase >5% in GPU memory footprint on steady-state workload
implementation_notes: Fair-spill policy: compute tenant-weighted LRU score and prefer spill-to-host over immediate eviction for fragments with touch_count < 3 and age < 90s
Compact-revivor: background agent coalesces adjacent fragment headers; uses atomic reservation to avoid conflicting rehydrations
Prefill-credit merging: merge credits across up to 8 microbatches and allow background merge to claim a portion of idle credit to perform non-blocking rehydration
Kernel-selection heuristic: expose FRAGMENT_PENALTY metric; if penalty > threshold, pick sparse-attention kernel; tie-breaker uses estimated compute cost vs. memory copy cost
Metrics to add: fragment_count_by_size, spilled_fragment_bytes, compact_merges_per_hour, kernel_hint_matches, prefill_credit_delays
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Increased host I/O could impact co-located services. Mitigation: use cgroups/io class and throttle; provide opt-out config per cluster.
Risk: Background compaction may introduce CPU/GPU jitter. Mitigation: schedule only when GPU idle < threshold and cap compaction throughput.
Risk: Starvation of foreground prefill by background merges. Mitigation: prefill admission token and credit isolation; run canary with strict SLO monitoring.
